sites.evidence_type: topology inference (C-terminal snorkel — no accessible terminus)
sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)
ordered surface loop (8 aa): pLDDT>=70, DSSP loop/turn, exposed junction residue (max RSA), indel-tolerant, 3D-clear of features

literature_notes: All eight ledger lines (L1–L8) describe a single published experiment: a V5 epitope tag introduced by CRISPR into the C-terminal tail of gjd4/Cx46.8 (GJD4) in zebrafish. The topology landmarks place the entire C-terminal tail (residues 218–370) in the intracellular compartment. The tag is therefore cytoplasmic, not extracellular, and does not qualify as a surface tag site. No ledger line reports any insertion in either extracellular loop (EL1: 45–76; EL2: 168–195) or at any extracellular terminus. Because the ledger contains no evidence of a tolerated extracellular tag insertion for GJD4, zero sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: V5 epitope tag inserted by CRISPR into a non-conserved region of the intracellular C-terminal tail (residues 218–370); protein is expressed and localises correctly in vivo, but the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
